title: Locally finitely presented flat sheaves are locally finite free retracts
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings and module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $N$ be a flat $\mathcal O$-module sheaf, meaning that $N\otimes_{\mathcal O}-$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Assume $N$ is locally finitely presented: for every $U\in\mathcal C$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and finite integers $r_i,s_i\ge0$ with an exact sequence $\mathcal O_{U_i}^{\oplus r_i}\to\mathcal O_{U_i}^{\oplus s_i}\to N|_{U_i}\to0$ in the abelian category of module sheaves. Restrictions and the ring sheaves $\mathcal O_{U_i}$ are those of the localized ringed sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Then for every $U\in\mathcal C$ there is a covering $\{V_j\to U\}$, integers $n_j\ge0$ and $\mathcal O_{V_j}$-linear sheaf maps $i_j:N|_{V_j}\to\mathcal O_{V_j}^{\oplus n_j}$ and $p_j:\mathcal O_{V_j}^{\oplus n_j}\to N|_{V_j}$ such that $p_ji_j=\operatorname{id}_{N|_{V_j}}$.

proof.text: Fix $U$. Use the locally finite presentation hypothesis to choose a covering $\{W_\alpha\to U\}$ and, on each $W=W_\alpha$, a presentation $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{A}\mathcal O_W^{\oplus s}\xrightarrow{q}N|_W\to0$. By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], the object $W/W$ is terminal in the slice and $(N|_W)(W/W)=N(W)$. A morphism $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus s}\to N|_W$ is specified by sections $u_1,\ldots,u_s\in N(W)$: on $T\to W$ it sends $(x_p)$ to $\sum_p x_p u_p|_T$, by the linearity and naturality in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Likewise $A$ is a matrix $(a_{pj})$ over $\mathcal O(W)$. Finite direct sums here have section groups given by finite tuples, since finite products of sheaves satisfy the sheaf axiom and are biproducts of module sheaves. The equality $qA=0$ reads $\sum_p a_{pj}u_p=0$ for every column $j$.

source.place: Tag 08FD (lemma-flat-locally-finite-presentation), choose the finite presentation; sectionwise reading of maps on the localized site

proof.text: We prove the following claim by induction on $m$, simultaneously for every object $W$ and every $n\ge0$: if $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{A}\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{g}N|_W$ has $gA=0$, there is a covering $\{V\to W\}$ on which $g=pB$, with $B:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus l}$ and $p:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus l}\to N|_V$ for a finite $l\ge0$, and $BA|_V=0$. For $m=0$, take the identity covering, $l=n$, $B=\operatorname{id}$, $p=g$. The identity covering is permitted by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Relocalization in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] identifies each further restriction with the restriction directly to $V$.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), proof of (2) implies (3), induction statement and base case

proof.text: For the induction step $m>0$, write $u_p=g(e_p)\in N(W)$ and let $(a_p)$ be the last column of $A$. The relation $\sum_p a_pu_p=0$ satisfies exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-relations-universes], applied to the original flat sheaf $N$ on $\mathcal C$ and the object $W$. This gives a covering $\{W_i\to W\}$, integers $l_i\ge0$, coefficients $b_{ipq}\in\mathcal O(W_i)$ and sections $t_{iq}\in N(W_i)$ such that $u_p|_{W_i}=\sum_q b_{ipq}t_{iq}$ and $\sum_p a_p|_{W_i}b_{ipq}=0$. Define $B_i(e_p)=\sum_q b_{ipq}e_q$ and $p_i(e_q)=t_{iq}$, extended by the sectionwise linear formulas of Step 1. Then $p_iB_i=g|_{W_i}$ and the last column of $B_iA|_{W_i}$ is zero. The criterion is used only for a single relation, exactly as its statement provides; no assertion about flatness of section modules is made.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), implication (1) to (2) and first part of the induction (2) to (3)

proof.text: Let $A_i'$ consist of the first $m-1$ columns of $B_iA|_{W_i}$. We have $p_iA_i'=0$, since $p_iB_iA|_{W_i}=gA|_{W_i}=0$. The induction hypothesis applies to $A_i',p_i$ on $W_i$, with source rank $m-1$ and middle rank $l_i$. Thus on a covering $\{V_{ih}\to W_i\}$ there are $C_{ih},p_{ih}$ with $p_{ih}C_{ih}=p_i|_{V_{ih}}$ and $C_{ih}A_i'|_{V_{ih}}=0$. Put $B_{ih}=C_{ih}B_i|_{V_{ih}}$. Its composite with $A|_{V_{ih}}$ kills the first $m-1$ columns by this equality and the last column because $B_iA|_{W_i}$ already kills it. Moreover $p_{ih}B_{ih}=p_i|_{V_{ih}}B_i|_{V_{ih}}=g|_{V_{ih}}$. The composite family $\{V_{ih}\to W\}$ covers by covering transitivity in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; restrictions compose by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. This completes the induction. All these are matrix compositions, the induction hypothesis and the covering axiom, not additional factorization lemmas.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), proof of (2) implies (3), induction on the number of columns

proof.text: Apply the finite-relation induction to the presentation from Step 1. Restriction along f:V→W is Mathlib's overMap. On underlying abelian sheaves it is pushforward along Over.map f, which is cocontinuous and continuous. Mathlib's sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous makes this functor a left adjoint, so it preserves colimits. The forgetful functor from module sheaves preserves colimits (the existing library instance preservesColimitsOfShape_toSheaf) and reflects them, so overMap preserves colimits as well. In particular the restricted presentation map remains the cokernel of the restricted relation map. The proof uses mapIsColimit on the presentation cofork and does not assume sectionwise surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 08FD (lemma-flat-locally-finite-presentation), finite-relation factorization; exact restriction on the localized ringed site

proof.text: Since $BA|_V=0$, the universal property of the cokernel $q|_V$ gives a unique module-sheaf map $i:N|_V\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus l}$ with $i(q|_V)=B$. It satisfies $(pi)(q|_V)=pB=q|_V$. A cokernel is an epimorphism, so cancellation gives $pi=\operatorname{id}_{N|_V}$. These are the defining universal properties of cokernel and epimorphism in the abelian module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. In particular we construct a section of $p$; no sectionwise lifting of sections through $q$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08FD (lemma-flat-locally-finite-presentation), final sentence, cokernel descent and the explicit section

proof.text: Compose the coverings $V\to W_\alpha\to U$ using [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. On each resulting member take $n_j=l$ and the maps $i_j=i$, $p_j=p$ just constructed. The identities $p_ji_j=\operatorname{id}$ give the required conclusion for the original arbitrary object $U$. The argument permits all ranks to be zero: for $r=0$ the induction uses the identity factorization; for $s=0$ the epimorphism $0\to N|_W$ forces $N|_W=0$, and the same cokernel argument works with rank zero. Empty covering families, when allowed by the topology, also cause no exception to the covering conclusion.

source.place: Tag 08FD (lemma-flat-locally-finite-presentation), compose local choices to obtain a covering of the original object

proof_origin.place: Tag 08FD (lemma-flat-locally-finite-presentation), using the explicit induction (2) to (3) in Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq); the cokernel section in the final sentence is written out. Lean implementation: use the independent-universe local relation criterion and establish preservation of colimits for overMap directly from the cocontinuous sheaf adjunction and the module-sheaf forgetful functor.
